disposition_mapping.rationale: Six of seven council seats held that the trial-balance-close confirmation must remain a discrete, loggable, dated gate distinct from adjustment posting; only maximalist proposed folding it into a merged close-and-adjust step and conceded the point was not decisive against the convergence. The underlying status aggregation is modernised into continuous automated monitoring (per finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect), but the confirmation itself remains a separately attributable human act satisfying KB-03's reporting-period discipline and FSP-R-01's ordering requirement, with any automation specified to run against batch extracts as well as live feeds per emerging_economy's deployment concern.

finance_domain's split between mechanical, rules-based postings and judgment-based estimation entries gained broad support (pragmatist, emerging_economy and hitl_designer each explicitly conceded or proposed the same split) on the grounds that estimation items otherwise hide inside an apparently-complete step, obscuring exactly the bottleneck a close manager needs visibility into. KB-04 and KB-10 require estimation entries to carry a documented basis and an accountable preparer that cannot be delegated to a system default; separating this into its own named step makes that accountability checkable rather than an internal attribute. Both resulting steps retain the approved adjustment schedule and revenue cut-off evidence inputs required by FSP-R-02 and FSP-R-06.

Strong convergence (pragmatist, finance_domain after concession, emerging_economy, maximalist, agentic_architect, hitl_designer, accounting_standards with conditions) supports combining consolidation/elimination with FX translation into one step, since both are deterministic computations over the same ledger data owned by the same scarce group-accounting skill set, with no requirement forcing a handoff between them. finance_domain's resequencing correction is adopted as a binding internal rule: translation executes before elimination so intercompany positions are matched on a consistent currency basis, per FSP-R-03 and FSP-R-04, and the elimination record remains a separately retrievable artifact per KB-14 and accounting_standards' condition.

Merged with FSP-03 into one consolidation-and-translation step for the reasons given there, but translation differences remain a separately labelled output (never netted into the consolidated figure), per KB-07, KB-08 and the explicit condition raised by accounting_standards, finance_domain and hitl_designer. FX anomaly review is retained as a visible human touchpoint inside the merged step, not collapsed into a generic 'review the output' task.

A clear majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) held that mapping must remain a visible, separately-gated step rather than being absorbed into drafting, because its failure mode — silent misclassification against an inconsistent chart of accounts — is precisely the kind of error a generative drafting pass will not reliably catch on its own. Mapping logic itself is automated as a mechanical, rules-evaluable transformation, consistent with accounting_standards' and maximalist's view that mapping carries low judgment content, but the exception-review checkpoint for new or unmapped accounts is kept explicit and owned by Financial Reporting, and the statement line-item structure remains an explicit input per FSP-R-05.

Universal agreement that drafting remains a distinct, human-owned activity per FSP-R-11; policy-change and prior-period-error disclosure (KB-05, KB-06) require judgment about materiality and presentation that cannot be delegated to a template or folded into an automated pipeline. Drafting tools may assist with boilerplate, but the accountable actor and the step boundary are unchanged, and the actor remains distinct from the approver per FSP-R-08.

Although unconstrained_by_design in the encoding, six of seven members (all but maximalist, who conceded in round 2) independently concluded this step must survive as a distinct function, because KB-02's evidential-trail principle and KB-05's error-correction principle both imply an independent check distinct from the act of drafting — a self-validating generative pass is not a second set of eyes. The step is modernised with automated tie-out tooling but retains genuine human analytical review, and is extended per finance_domain's and agentic_architect's acknowledged gap to explicitly classify discrepancies as current-period fixes versus IAS 8 prior-period errors, feeding the latter back into drafting's error record.

Unanimous: management review and approval survives unchanged in substance per FSP-R-09, structurally separated from drafting per FSP-R-08, which is treated as an absolute requirement with no compensating-control substitute (contra emerging_economy's thin-headcount accommodation, which accounting_standards correctly notes has no basis in the knowledge base as equivalent to actual separation). The council's shared refinement — that the approval package must surface the upstream exception and judgment trail rather than only a polished output — is adopted so the approval is substantive rather than ceremonial.

The council split on whether release should merge with approval (maximalist alone) or remain distinct (pragmatist, finance_domain, agentic_architect, emerging_economy, hitl_designer). The majority view is adopted: approval is an internal attestation event and release is an external, often irreversible act creating third-party reliance, and collapsing them removes the gap in which audit-opinion finalisation, board ratification, or filing-window checks occur. Release mechanics are automated but strictly trigger-gated on the logged approval event, with a byte-for-byte approved-vs-filed match check and an offline/manual fallback path per emerging_economy's deployment non-negotiable.

steps.actor: GL accountant (supported by close-readiness monitoring automation)
steps.description: Subledger close status and reconciliation completeness are continuously monitored via automated dashboards; the GL accountant reviews the resulting exception list and issues a discrete, timestamped confirmation that the trial balance is closed and reconciled before any adjustment posting begins. The confirmation remains a separately loggable, attestable event, not an internal flag inside a larger automated process.
steps.name: Continuous close monitoring and trial balance confirmation gate
outputs: Closed reconciled trial balance (dated, attributable confirmation record)

steps.actor: GL accountant (adjustment-posting automation under accountant oversight)
steps.description: Rules-based, schedule-driven entries (standard accruals, deferral releases, routine cut-off postings) are posted automatically from the approved adjustment schedule and verified revenue cut-off evidence. All postings are reversible through a standard protocol, never one-way writes, so error correction remains possible.
steps.name: Post mechanical period-end adjustments

steps.description: Estimation-based entries (provisions, impairments, NRV write-downs, expected credit losses) are prepared by a named accountable preparer with a documented basis attached before posting, reviewed, and posted, yielding the final adjusted trial balance. This function is kept visibly distinct from mechanical posting so a judgment bottleneck is never hidden inside a step that looks otherwise complete.
steps.name: Prepare and post judgmental estimation entries

steps.description: Each foreign subsidiary's trial balance is translated to the presentation currency at closing and average rates first; intercompany balances and transactions are then matched and eliminated on the resulting common-currency basis, so eliminations are never struck across inconsistent currency bases. Unmatched intercompany items, stale or missing rates, and anomalous translation movements are routed to the group accountant for resolution rather than auto-cleared. Translation differences and the elimination record remain separately retrievable artifacts, never netted into a single black-box consolidated figure.
steps.name: Translate foreign operations and consolidate with intercompany elimination

steps.description: An automated mapping engine classifies consolidated and translated balances against the maintained chart-of-accounts-to-line-item taxonomy. New, reclassified, or unrecognized accounts are exception-routed to a named Financial Reporting reviewer rather than defaulted or silently dropped, preserving a visible checkpoint against misclassification in inconsistent charts of accounts.
steps.name: Map trial balance to statement line items

steps.description: Financial reporting drafts the primary statements and key notes, including disclosure of accounting policy changes and prior-period errors, assisted by drafting tools for boilerplate and comparatives but owning all judgmental disclosure content and materiality decisions.
inputs: Accounting policy change and prior-period error record
steps.name: Draft primary statements and key notes

steps.actor: Financial reporting (reviewer distinct from the preparer of the draft where feasible)
steps.description: A reviewer, assisted by automated tie-out tooling, ties the draft statements to the trial balance and supporting schedules and performs genuine analytical review of variances and plausibility rather than merely adjudicating system-flagged exceptions. This remains a distinct step, functionally separate from drafting, because a check performed by the same act that produced the draft is not an independent check. Discrepancies are explicitly triaged and classified as current-period corrections or IAS 8 prior-period errors, with the latter feeding back into the drafting step's error record.
steps.name: Analytical review and tie-out
outputs: Classified correction record (current-period fix vs. prior-period error)

steps.description: The CFO reviews and approves the financial statements. The review package explicitly surfaces the judgment and exception trail generated upstream — estimation bases, intercompany/FX exceptions, mapping exceptions, tie-out variances and error classifications — not only the finished statement set, so that approval reflects a reviewed trail of resolved judgments rather than sign-off on a polished artifact with no visible decision history. The approver is structurally distinct from the drafter at all times.
steps.name: Management review and approval

steps.actor: CFO (release confirmed via gated release function)
steps.description: Release and distribution mechanics (filing, tagging, investor distribution) are automated but strictly trigger-gated on the logged approval event from management review, never fired on a schedule or inference. The release function confirms a byte-for-byte match between the approved and filed/distributed package before release, with a manual/offline fallback path preserved where e-filing portals or network links are unreliable, and any failure blocks and escalates rather than retrying silently.
steps.name: Release / submission
